_comment_phr: yourPHR's phr add-on (jwilleke/yourphr#920). Merged into the site's configuration only while ngdpbase.addons.phr.enabled is true; the site's app-custom-config.json overrides any entry.
_comment_phr_site_critical: yourPHR can't work without phr: any failure to load puts the whole site in maintenance mode, and admins get the reason (operator decision 2026-10-18, ngdpbase#1883). A site may turn this off in its own configuration; it then owns that risk.
_comment_phr_database: phr.db: health records under the site's database key (D2). encrypt "required": core never opens it without NGDPBASE_DATABASE_KEY (D3), and with site-critical the site goes into maintenance instead (ngdpbase#1860, #1883).
_comment_phr_vault: One PHR vault per user (operator, 2026-10-15; ngdpbase#1559). owner, encrypt, defaultPrivate and shareMaxDays are phr's own and a site can't override them. encrypt is fixed when each user's vault is created. Booleans must be booleans: core refuses to load phr otherwise. Comments and footnotes are off on phr's categories (ngdpbase#1952): a user's notes about a record go into phr.db as patient-entered data, never into core's shared comment tabs. phr-pages holds phr's shared, non-PHI pages.

phr-pages.label: phr-pages
phr-pages.description: yourPHR's own pages (no health data in them: records are drawn per user from phr.db)

_comment_step_up: No phr permission is marked "step-up": true (operator decision 2026-10-18): add-ons keep step-up off for now, because a form loses its fields across the fresh sign-in. Core's own step-up window is 60 minutes.

phr-read.description: Read one's own health records in the phr add-on (or a represented user's, under a proxy grant)
phr-read.label: See my health records

audit.description: Health records read: who, whose (owner), which kind and id; never content

phr-write.description: Add or update one's own health records in the phr add-on
phr-write.label: Add to my health records

audit.description: Health record added or updated: who, whose (owner), which kind and id; never content

phr-delete.description: Remove one's own health records in the phr add-on
phr-delete.label: Remove from my health records

audit.description: Health record removed: who, whose (owner), which kind and id

phr-migrate.description: Move each user's records from yourPHR into their own health record, once, at cutover (yourphr#969). Held only by the scheduled job phr.migrate-yourphr
phr-migrate.label: Move records in from yourPHR

audit.description: Health record moved in from yourPHR: which job, whose (owner), which kind and id; never content

ngdpbase.access.policies.name: Health records
ngdpbase.access.policies.description: Who may use phr at all: every user, through the role vault-owner that every account holds (ngdpbase#1539, operator 2026-10-24: a permission over a user's own records goes to vault-owner, never to site roles). Whose records a user may see is not decided here: phr reads each record's owner from storage and core decides (owner rule, then policy). The resource type becomes phr-record once phr declares it (ngdpbase#1823).

ngdpbase.access.policies.name: phr: the move in from yourPHR
ngdpbase.access.policies.description: The scheduled job phr.migrate-yourphr alone may write each user's records from yourPHR into that user's own health record, until cutover is done; then the job and this policy go (yourphr#969, operator 2026-10-25). It also reads each old user's identity record (identity-read) to find the identity @id phr keys records by. No role holds phr-migrate.
